<p class="hero-title">Veterinary epidemiologist using Bayesian models to estimate how livestock diseases spread and where control will work best.</p>

<p>I am a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) graduate and an MS candidate in Medicine at the Department of Medicine, Bangladesh Agricultural University.</p>

<p>My research uses Bayesian statistics to answer practical questions about livestock disease: how common an infection really is when diagnostic tests are imperfect, how fast it spreads within herds, where it is likely to go next, and which control measures are worth their cost. Most of my work so far has been on dairy cattle (brucellosis, paratuberculosis, Q fever, neosporosis, bovine viral diarrhoea and subclinical mastitis). My MS thesis now applies these methods to African swine fever in free-ranging pigs.</p>

<p>I work in the Epidemiology &amp; Preventive Medicine Lab under <a href="https://vm.bau.edu.bd/teachers/VM1004" target="_blank"><strong>A.K.M. Anisur Rahman</strong></a>. My work combines farm sampling and laboratory diagnostics (ELISA, PCR) with model building in R and Stan and disease mapping in QGIS.</p>

<div class="thesis-card">
  <span class="thesis-eyebrow">Current Research · MS Thesis (In Progress)</span>
  <p class="thesis-title">Bayesian Quantitative Risk Assessment of African Swine Fever Spread among Scavenging Pig Populations in Bangladesh</p>
  <p>African swine fever (genotype II) reached Bangladesh in 2023 and 2024, where most pigs are kept by marginalised communities in free-ranging and nomadic systems. Following the WOAH risk analysis framework, I am estimating within-herd R₀ from outbreak data, the yearly probability that the virus reaches new districts, how much spread could go undetected, and which controls (border checks, heat-treating swill, faster reporting) would reduce risk most.</p>
  <p class="thesis-meta">Master of Science in Medicine · April 2025 – Present · Department of Medicine, Bangladesh Agricultural University<br>
  Supervisor: <a href="https://vm.bau.edu.bd/teachers/VM1004" target="_blank">Prof. Dr. A.K.M. Anisur Rahman</a> · CGPA 3.80 / 4.00 (first semester)</p>
</div>

<p>You can find my publications, research projects, data visualizations and CV through the menu above.</p>

<h2>Key Highlights</h2>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Nine peer-reviewed journal articles</strong> published, three as first or equally contributing first author, and <strong>five manuscripts under review</strong>, including in <em>Epidemics</em>, <em>Preventive Veterinary Medicine</em> and <em>Veterinary Medicine and Science</em>.</li>
  <li>Applied <strong>Bayesian latent-class prevalence estimation, catalytic force-of-infection models, mixture-model test cut-offs and decision-analytic economic models</strong> to six infectious diseases in large Bangladeshi dairy herds.</li>
  <li><strong>Leading an independent global research programme on human brucellosis</strong> with a ten-member team, using Bayesian meta-analysis and spatiotemporal mapping.</li>
  <li>Recipient of the <strong>National Science and Technology (NST) Fellowship 2026</strong>.</li>
</ul>
